items.title: A $400,000 Portfolio in Comcast, Hormel and AT&T Pays $20,500 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA $400,000 portfolio split evenly across Comcast, Hormel Foods and AT&T pays about $20,500 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $1,710 a month. Comcast’s dividend is the best covered of the three, taking 24% of its free cash flow over the last twelve months, against 44% for AT&T and 82% for Hormel.

items.title: A $1,500,000 Portfolio in Realty Income, Comcast and Hormel Pays $79,746 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical $1,500,000 portfolio split evenly across Realty Income, Comcast and Hormel Foods pays about $79,700 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $6,650 a month. Realty Income and Comcast cover their dividends comfortably, at 75% of AFFO and 24% of free cash flow.

items.title: Disney Just Raised Its Dividend 33%, Giving Shareholders a Bigger Payday
items.summary: Disney's payout now beats anything it paid before the 2020 suspension, yet buybacks and a $26 billion content bill still compete for the same cash. Does the bigger check turn a media giant into an income stock?
